<reason>Both sides argued the motion as written and kept the clash tight. PRO's core mechanism — insurance that lapses at the moment the claim arrives, because illness ends work — was conceded by CON in its opening and never dislodged. CON's main defence was that the hole is already patched (COBRA, exchanges, Medicaid) and that plural payers beat monopoly lock. PRO's Q1 turned that defence into a liability: asked to name a real exit for a 55-year-old whose cancer ended her ability to work, CON answered "subsidized exchange coverage," conceding that the operative backstop for the sick is already public financing. PRO's closing crystallised this cleanly ("doors count only if you can walk through them; the healthy have exits, the sick have applications"), which directly dismantles CON's "floor with doors" metaphor rather than merely restating earlier material. CON's best work was real: the turn on PRO's rescue list (France multi-payer, Australia's subsidised private layer, Medicare Advantage) genuinely damaged PRO's "floor plus layers" comparison, and Vermont/Colorado applied honest pressure on price. But PRO answered Vermont well and specifically (ERISA, the untouched federal tax preference, cross-border mobility, plus Medicare's political immovability), and CON's "relabeling, not saving" reply never engaged PRO's premiums-are-already-wages framing. CON's monopoly-budget-risk argument stays partly live but was weighed less persuasively than PRO's contrast between collectively contestable risk and individually correlated risk. PRO's Rebuttal 2 was clipped for length — a real but small execution cost that did not remove its substance. Format compliance (A1/A2, Q1/Q2) was good on both sides.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Pressure Question about the 55-year-old whose cancer ends her ability to work, followed by CON's answer "her exit is subsidized exchange coverage." That answer conceded that the only functioning door for the sick under employer-based coverage is public financing, letting PRO reframe the debate as public floor versus public trapdoor and collapse CON's "competing payers" advantage into an argument available mainly to the healthy and employed.</best_rebuttal>
